source.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς γένηται ἁπαλὸς καὶ τὰ φύλλα ἐκφύῃ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος·

records.literal_gloss: From but the fig tree learn the parable: when already the branch of it becomes tender and the leaves it puts out, you know that near the summer;

en.L: Now from the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer [is] near.
en.B: Take the fig tree as your lesson. When its branches turn soft and leaves start to sprout, you can tell that summer is not far off.
en.R: Learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches become green and soft and new leaves start to grow, you know that summer is coming soon.

es.L: Y de la higuera {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} la parábola: cuando ya su rama se pone tierna y echa las hojas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que cerca [está] el verano.
es.B: {{plural_you:Aprendan|Aprended}} la lección de la higuera: cuando sus ramas se ponen tiernas y empiezan a brotar las hojas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que el verano no está lejos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Aprendan|Aprended}} una lección de la higuera. Cuando sus ramas se ponen verdes y tiernas, y le salen hojas nuevas, {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que el verano llega pronto.

fr.L: Or, du figuier apprenez la parabole : dès que sa branche devient tendre et qu’elle pousse ses feuilles, vous savez que l’été est proche.
fr.B: Que le figuier vous serve de leçon. Quand ses rameaux deviennent souples et que ses feuilles commencent à pousser, vous savez que l’été n’est pas loin.
fr.R: Le figuier vous donne une leçon. Quand ses branches deviennent vertes et souples et que de nouvelles feuilles commencent à pousser, vous savez que l’été arrive bientôt.

sw.L: Basi kutoka kwa mtini jifunzeni mfano: tawi lake likishakuwa laini na kutoa majani, mnajua kwamba kiangazi [kiko] karibu.
sw.B: Jifunzeni somo kutoka kwa mtini: matawi yake yanapoanza kuwa laini na majani kuchipua, mnajua kwamba kiangazi kimekaribia.
sw.R: Jifunzeni somo kutoka kwa mtini. Matawi yake yanapokuwa mabichi na laini, na majani mapya yanapoanza kuchipua, mnajua kwamba kiangazi kinakuja hivi karibuni.

vi.L: Vậy hãy học ngụ ngôn từ cây vả: khi cành nó đã trở nên non mềm và nảy lá, các con biết rằng mùa hè đã gần.
vi.B: Hãy học lấy ngụ ngôn từ cây vả. Khi cành vả trở nên mềm mại và nảy lộc, các con biết mùa hè sắp đến.
vi.R: Hãy học một bài học từ cây vả. Khi cành của nó trở nên mềm và xanh, lá non bắt đầu mọc ra, các con biết mùa hè sắp đến.

ko.L: 그런데 무화과나무에서 비유를 배워라. 그 가지가 이미 연해지고 잎들을 내면, 너희는 여름이 가까운 줄 안다.
ko.B: 무화과나무에서 교훈을 배워라. 가지가 부드러워지고 잎이 돋으면, 너희는 여름이 가까이 온 줄 안다.
ko.R: 무화과나무에서 한 가지 교훈을 배워라. 가지가 부드럽고 푸르게 되고 새 잎이 돋기 시작하면, 너희는 곧 여름이 온다는 것을 안다.

am.L: ከበለስም ምሳሌውን ተማሩ፤ ቅርንጫፏ አሁን ለስላሳ ሲሆንና ቅጠሎችን ስታወጣ፣ በጋ እንደ ቀረበ ታውቃላችሁ።
am.B: ከበለስ ትምህርት ውሰዱ። ቅርንጫፎቿ ሲለሰልሱና ቅጠሎቿ ማቆጥቆጥ ሲጀምሩ በጋ ሩቅ እንዳልሆነ ታውቃላችሁ።
am.R: ከበለስ ዛፍ አንድ ትምህርት ተማሩ። ቅርንጫፎቿ ሲለመልሙና አዲስ ቅጠሎች ማብቀል ሲጀምሩ በጋ በቅርቡ እንደሚመጣ ታውቃላችሁ።

decisions.choice: the fig tree's leaves: a sign that summer is near
decisions.reason: Many trees in the land of Israel keep their leaves all year. The fig loses its leaves in winter, and new ones come in late spring, so its leaves show that summer is near.

decisions.choice: the parable: a comparison that teaches a lesson
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short comparison from nature.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: perhaps recalling the fig tree of 21:18-21
decisions.reason: Earlier a fig tree without fruit withered at Jesus's word. Here the fig tree's new leaves show that something is near.

decisions.choice: lesson
decisions.reason: Here the word means the lesson the fig tree teaches.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (aprendan|aprended, saben|sabéis)
decisions.reason: Jesus is speaking to his disciples (24:3), so every plural "you" in the passage is the ustedes / vosotros setting, a choice English does not have. The same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: kiangazi (the hot, dry season)
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel summer is the hot, dry season after the rains (meaning decision m1). "Kiangazi" is that season in East Africa; "majira ya joto" is a description borrowed from countries with four seasons.

decisions.choice: "bài học" (R); "ngụ ngôn" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a lesson drawn from the fig tree, not a story (meaning decision); Readable says "bài học", as the English Readable says "lesson", and as Mark 13:28 does. Literal and Balanced keep the Gospels' word for a parable, as Mark 13:28 and Luke 21:29 do.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 24:32-51; Jesus speaks in 해라체 and speaks of himself as "인자" and "주" with no honorific
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "비유" (L); "교훈" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short comparison that teaches a lesson (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say "교훈", as the English says "lesson" and the Korean Mark 13:28 Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ምሳሌ" (parable, L); "ትምህርት" (lesson, B, R); "በጋ" (the dry season) for summer
alternatives: "ክረምት" for the season the leaves announce
decisions.reason: The fig tree's leaves come in late spring, before the hot dry season, which is what "በጋ" means in Ethiopia. "ክረምት" is the rainy season (24:20), so it cannot stand for summer here.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε πάντα ταῦτα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.

records.literal_gloss: So also you, when you see all these things, know that near it is, at doors.

en.L: So also you, when you see all these things, know that [it] is near, at [the] doors.
en.B: So it is with you: once you see all these things, be sure that it is close, standing at the door.
en.R: In the same way, when you see all these things happen, you can be sure that the time is near. It is as close as someone standing at the door.

es.L: Así también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} todas estas cosas, {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} que está cerca, a [las] puertas.
es.B: Así también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} todas estas cosas, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} por seguro que está cerca, ya a la puerta.
es.R: Del mismo modo, cuando {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} que pasan todas estas cosas, {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros de que el momento está cerca. Está tan cerca como alguien que ya está a la puerta.

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, quand vous verrez toutes ces choses, sachez que [c’]est proche, aux portes.
fr.B: Il en est de même pour vous : quand vous verrez tout cela, soyez sûrs que c’est proche, juste à la porte.
fr.R: De la même façon, quand vous verrez toutes ces choses arriver, vous pourrez être sûrs que le moment est proche. Il est aussi près que quelqu’un qui se tient à la porte.

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo nanyi, mtakapoyaona haya yote, jueni kwamba ni karibu, milangoni.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo nanyi: mtakapoyaona mambo haya yote, jueni kwamba ni karibu, mlangoni kabisa.
sw.R: Vivyo hivyo, mtakapoona mambo haya yote yakitokea, mjue kwamba wakati umekaribia. Uko karibu kama mtu aliyesimama mlangoni.

vi.L: Cũng vậy, các con, khi thấy tất cả những điều này, hãy biết rằng [điều ấy] đã gần, ở ngay trước cửa.
vi.B: Các con cũng vậy: khi thấy tất cả những điều này, hãy biết chắc rằng điều ấy đã gần, ngay trước cửa rồi.
vi.R: Cũng vậy, khi các con thấy tất cả những điều này xảy ra, các con có thể biết chắc rằng thời điểm ấy đã gần. Nó đã gần như người đứng ngay trước cửa.

ko.L: 이와 같이 너희도 이 모든 일을 보거든, [그것이] 가까이, 문들 앞에 와 있는 줄 알아라.
ko.B: 마찬가지로 너희도 이 모든 일을 보면, 그것이 가까이 왔다는 것을, 바로 문 앞에 와 있다는 것을 알아라.
ko.R: 이와 같이 이 모든 일이 일어나는 것을 보면, 그때가 가까이 왔다는 것을 알아라. 그때는 문 앞에 서 있는 사람처럼 아주 가까이 와 있다.

am.L: እንዲሁ እናንተም ይህን ሁሉ ስታዩ፣ ቅርብ እንደ ሆነ፣ በደጆች ላይ እንዳለ እወቁ።
am.B: እናንተም እንደዚሁ ናችሁ፤ ይህን ሁሉ ስታዩ፣ ቅርብ እንደ ሆነና በደጅ እንደ ቆመ እርግጠኞች ሁኑ።
am.R: በዚህ ዓይነት እናንተም ይህ ሁሉ ሲሆን ስታዩ ጊዜው እንደ ቀረበ እርግጠኞች ሁኑ። በር ላይ እንደ ቆመ ሰው ቅርብ ነው።

decisions.choice: it is near: the subject is not stated; the end, or the coming of the Son of Man
alternatives: he is near: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject, so it can mean "it is near" or "he is near". Luke 21:31 says "the kingdom of God is near". The coming of 24:30 is what is near in either reading.

decisions.choice: all these things: the troubles and signs of 24:4-28
alternatives: the darkening of the sun and the coming itself
decisions.reason: "These things" are what come before the end, as in the disciples' question (24:3).

decisions.choice: at the doors: very close
alternatives: at the doors of the temple
decisions.reason: To be at the door is to be about to come in.

decisions.choice: the time is near
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject as the time of these events, which keeps both readings open as far as English allows.

decisions.choice: ni karibu (it is near), with no subject
decisions.reason: The Greek does not say what is near (meaning decision m1). A Swahili subject prefix names the class of its subject: "yu karibu" would decide for the Son of Man and "iko karibu" for a thing. "Ni karibu" leaves the subject open, as the Greek does; Readable says "wakati" (the time), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "[điều ấy]" (L); "điều ấy" (B); "thời điểm ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the subject unstated (footnoted meaning decision); "điều ấy" keeps it as open as the Greek, as in Mark 13:29.

decisions.choice: [그것이] (L); "그것이" (B); "그때가" (R)
decisions.reason: The subject is not stated (meaning decision, footnoted). As in the Korean Mark 13:29, "그것" leaves both readings open; Readable says "그때", as the English Readable says "the time".

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα ταῦτα γένηται.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you that not not will pass away the generation this until all these things happen.

en.L: Truly I tell you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things take place.
en.B: Truly I tell you, all these things will happen before this generation has passed away.
en.R: I tell you the truth: the people living now will not all die before all these things happen.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que de ningún modo pasará esta generación hasta que todas estas cosas sucedan.
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que todo esto sucederá antes de que pase esta generación.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: antes de que muera toda la gente que vive ahora, sucederán todas estas cosas.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis : cette génération ne passera certainement pas jusqu’à ce que toutes ces choses soient arrivées.
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : tout cela arrivera avant que cette génération ait passé.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : les gens qui vivent aujourd’hui ne seront pas tous morts avant que tout cela arrive.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia kwamba kizazi hiki hakitapita kamwe hadi mambo haya yote yatokee.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, mambo haya yote yatatokea kabla kizazi hiki hakijapita.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: watu wanaoishi sasa hawatakufa wote kabla mambo haya yote hayajatokea.

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con rằng thế hệ này chắc chắn sẽ không qua đi cho đến khi tất cả những điều này xảy ra.
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, tất cả những điều này sẽ xảy ra trước khi thế hệ này qua đi.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: tất cả những điều này sẽ xảy ra trước khi những người đang sống bây giờ qua đời hết.

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 이 모든 일이 일어날 때까지 이 세대는 결코 지나가지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 이 세대가 지나가기 전에 이 모든 일이 일어날 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 지금 살아 있는 사람들이 다 죽기 전에 이 모든 일이 일어날 것이다.

am.L: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ ይህ ሁሉ እስኪፈጸም ድረስ ይህ ትውልድ በምንም ዓይነት አያልፍም።
am.B: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ ይህ ትውልድ ከማለፉ በፊት ይህ ሁሉ ይፈጸማል።
am.R: እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ፣ አሁን የሚኖሩት ሰዎች ሁሉ ከመሞታቸው በፊት ይህ ሁሉ ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living in Jesus's own time
alternatives: the generation that sees the signs
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Matthew "this generation" means Jesus's contemporaries (11:16; 12:41-45; 23:36). Others take it as the people of Israel or the generation alive when the signs begin. The meaning depends on what "all these things" includes.

decisions.choice: all these things: the events of 24:4-28, including the fall of the temple
alternatives: everything in the speech, including the coming of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: "All these things" in 24:33 are the signs that come before the end. Read that way, Jesus says his own generation will see them, while the day itself no one knows (24:36).

decisions.choice: will certainly not: a double negative, a firm promise
decisions.reason: The strongest form of denial.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as in 24:2.

decisions.choice: the people living now
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading chosen above. If that reading is wrong, this wording says more than the Greek.

decisions.choice: En verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single "amen" used through Matthew; it covers 24:47.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis : (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
alternatives: En vérité, je vous dis que (L)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for the "amen" saying, as in Mark 13:30; Literal too uses the fixed formula and a colon rather than "que". The same in 24:47 and 25:12, 25:40, 25:45.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single "amen" used through Matthew, as John's double form is "Kweli kweli nawaambia"; it covers 24:47.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R); "이 세대" (L, B), "지금 살아 있는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, as at 24:2; "이 세대" and its Readable wording follow the Korean Mark 13:30.

decisions.choice: "እውነት እላችኋለሁ" (L, B); "እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's "amen" before his own words means "this is true". "አሜን" in Amharic closes a prayer and would be misheard, so Literal and Balanced say "truly I tell you" and Readable "I tell you the truth"; Literal gives the Greek double negative as "በምንም ዓይነት" (in no way).

source.text: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσεται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρέλθωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: The heaven and the earth will pass away, the but words of me not not will pass away.

en.L: Heaven and earth will pass away, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will certainly not pass away.
en.B: Heaven and earth will pass away; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words never will.
en.R: The sky and the earth will come to an end, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will last forever.

es.L: El cielo y la tierra pasarán, pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras de ningún modo pasarán.
es.B: El cielo y la tierra pasarán; {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras, jamás.
es.R: El cielo y la tierra llegarán a su fin, pero {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras durarán para siempre.

fr.L: Le ciel et la terre passeront, mais {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles ne passeront certainement pas.
fr.B: Le ciel et la terre passeront ; {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, elles, ne passeront jamais.
fr.R: Le ciel et la terre vont finir, mais {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles dureront pour toujours.

sw.L: Mbingu na dunia zitapita, lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hayatapita kwa vyovyote.
sw.B: Mbingu na dunia zitapita, ila maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hayatapita kamwe.
sw.R: Mbingu na dunia zitafikia mwisho, lakini maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yatadumu milele.

vi.L: Trời và đất sẽ qua đi, nhưng các lời của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn sẽ không qua đi.
vi.B: Trời đất sẽ qua đi, nhưng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không bao giờ qua đi.
vi.R: Trời và đất sẽ không còn nữa, nhưng lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ còn mãi mãi.

ko.L: 하늘과 땅은 지나갈 것이다. 그러나 내 말들은 결코 지나가지 않을 것이다.
ko.B: 하늘과 땅은 사라지겠지만, 내 말은 결코 사라지지 않을 것이다.
ko.R: 하늘과 땅은 언젠가 끝날 것이다. 그러나 내 말은 영원히 남을 것이다.

am.L: ሰማይና ምድር ያልፋሉ፤ ቃሎቼ ግን በምንም ዓይነት አያልፉም።
am.B: ሰማይና ምድር ያልፋሉ፤ ቃሎቼ ግን ከቶ አያልፉም።
am.R: ሰማይና ምድር ይጠፋሉ፤ ቃሎቼ ግን ለዘላለም ይኖራሉ።

decisions.choice: heaven and earth pass, my words remain: as God's word stands forever
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40:8 says the word of our God stands forever, and Isaiah 51:6 says the heavens will vanish like smoke. Jesus says of his own words what the prophets said of God's word (compare 5:18).

decisions.choice: will certainly not pass away: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strongest denial: his words will never fail.

decisions.choice: come to an end; last forever
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for passing away and never passing away.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (mis)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves most subject pronouns out and marks the person in the verb, where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English (24:44 Readable has none). The same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span on yangu (my) only
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns with a prefix inside the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. In 24:44 the English Readable marks "he"; Swahili says "atakuja" with no span. The same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: "지나가다" (L), as in 24:34
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the same verb for the generation and for heaven and earth; Literal keeps one Korean verb for both, as the Korean Mark 13:31 does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans: the suffix "-ኤ" (my) in "ቃሎቼ" stays as it is
alternatives: a capitalised pronoun, as the English alternative
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic. The English spans in this passage have no Amharic counterpart.

source.text: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ μόνος.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning but the day that and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens nor the Son, except the Father alone.

en.L: But concerning that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
en.B: No one knows the day or the hour when that will come. The angels in heaven do not know it, and neither does the Son. Only the Father knows.
en.R: But no one knows on what day or at what hour this will happen. The angels in heaven do not know. Even the Son does not know. Only the Father knows.

es.L: Pero acerca de aquel día y hora nadie sabe, ni los ángeles de los cielos, ni el Hijo, sino solo el Padre.
es.B: Nadie sabe el día ni la hora en que eso llegará. No lo saben los ángeles del cielo, ni tampoco el Hijo. Solo el Padre lo sabe.
es.R: Pero nadie sabe qué día ni a qué hora sucederá esto. Los ángeles del cielo no lo saben. Ni siquiera el Hijo lo sabe. Solo el Padre lo sabe.

fr.L: Mais au sujet de ce jour-là et de l’heure, personne ne sait, pas même les anges des cieux, ni le Fils, sinon le Père seul.
fr.B: Personne ne connaît le jour ni l’heure où cela arrivera. Les anges du ciel ne les connaissent pas, et le Fils non plus. Seul le Père les connaît.
fr.R: Mais personne ne sait quel jour ni à quelle heure cela arrivera. Les anges dans le ciel ne le savent pas. Même le Fils ne le sait pas. Seul le Père le sait.

sw.L: Lakini kuhusu siku ile na saa hakuna anayejua, wala malaika wa mbinguni, wala Mwana, isipokuwa Baba peke yake.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu anayejua siku wala saa jambo hilo litakapotokea. Malaika walio mbinguni hawajui, wala Mwana hajui. Baba peke yake ndiye anayejua.
sw.R: Lakini hakuna mtu anayejua ni siku gani au saa ngapi jambo hili litatokea. Malaika wa mbinguni hawajui. Hata Mwana hajui. Baba peke yake ndiye anayejua.

vi.L: Nhưng về ngày đó và giờ đó thì không ai biết, ngay cả các thiên sứ trên các tầng trời, ngay cả Con cũng không, chỉ một mình Cha [biết] mà thôi.
vi.B: Còn về ngày ấy và giờ ấy thì không ai biết. Các thiên sứ trên trời không biết, và Con cũng không biết. Chỉ một mình Cha biết mà thôi.
vi.R: Nhưng không ai biết ngày nào hay giờ nào việc này sẽ xảy ra. Các thiên sứ trên trời không biết. Ngay cả Con cũng không biết. Chỉ có Cha biết mà thôi.

ko.L: 그러나 그 날과 그 때에 대해서는 아무도 모른다. 하늘들의 천사들도 모르고, 아들도 모르고, 오직 아버지만 아신다.
ko.B: 그 날이나 그 때가 언제 올지는 아무도 모른다. 하늘의 천사들도 모르고 아들도 모른다. 오직 아버지께서만 아신다.
ko.R: 그러나 이 일이 어느 날, 어느 때에 일어날지는 아무도 모른다. 하늘에 있는 천사들도 모른다. 아들조차도 모른다. 오직 아버지께서만 아신다.

am.L: ስለዚያ ቀንና ሰዓት ግን ማንም አያውቅም፤ የሰማያት መላእክት እንኳ አያውቁም፣ ወልድም [አያውቅም]፤ ከአብ ብቻ በቀር።
am.B: ያ የሚሆንበትን ቀንና ሰዓት ማንም አያውቅም። በሰማይ ያሉ መላእክት አያውቁትም፤ ወልድም አያውቀውም። የሚያውቀው አብ ብቻ ነው።
am.R: ይህ በየትኛው ቀንና በየትኛው ሰዓት እንደሚሆን ማንም አያውቅም። በሰማይ ያሉ መላእክት አያውቁም። ልጁም እንኳ አያውቅም። የሚያውቀው አባት ብቻ ነው።

decisions.choice: nor the Son, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: "Nor the Son" is in some of the earliest manuscripts, such as Codex Sinaiticus as first written and Codex Vaticanus, and is missing from many later ones, perhaps because copyists found it hard. Nearly all manuscripts have it in Mark 13:32. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: nor the Son: Jesus says that he, the Son, does not know the day
alternatives: the Son knows but will not tell
decisions.reason: The Father alone has set the day. The text does not explain how the Son, who shares the Father's knowledge (11:27), does not know it while he lives among people.

decisions.choice: that day and hour: the time of the Son of Man's coming
alternatives: the day of the temple's fall
decisions.reason: "That day" is the prophets' phrase for the day of the Lord. Here it is the day of the coming described in 24:30-31.

decisions.choice: when that will come (B); this will happen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the list into short sentences and say what the day is.

decisions.choice: "Con" and "Cha", capitalised, with no setting
decisions.reason: As in Mark 13:32 and John: nouns for the Son and the Father, always capitalised; the style guide gives them no setting span.

decisions.choice: "아들도 모른다" with no honorific; "아버지께서만 아신다" with it
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 13:32: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son and does not honour himself; he honours the Father.

decisions.choice: "ወልድ" and "አብ" (the Son, the Father, L, B); "ልጁ" and "አባት" (R)
decisions.reason: Used absolutely, "the Son" and "the Father" are the names Amharic readers know from the church, "ወልድ" and "አብ". Readable uses the everyday words, which say the same relationship.

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

records.literal_gloss: Just as for the days of the Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of the Man;

en.L: For just as the days of Noah [were], so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
en.B: The coming of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.
en.R: When the Son of Man comes, it will be like it was in the time of Noah.

es.L: Porque como [fueron] los días de Noé, así será la venida del Hijo del Hombre.
es.B: La venida del Hijo del Hombre será como los días de Noé.
es.R: Cuando venga el Hijo del Hombre, será como en el tiempo de Noé.

fr.L: Car comme [ont été] les jours de Noé, ainsi sera la venue du Fils de l’homme.
fr.B: La venue du Fils de l’homme sera comme au temps de Noé.
fr.R: Quand le Fils de l’homme viendra, ce sera comme au temps de Noé.

sw.L: Kwa maana kama siku za Nuhu [zilivyokuwa], hivyo ndivyo kuja kwa Mwana wa Adamu kutakavyokuwa.
sw.B: Kuja kwa Mwana wa Adamu kutakuwa kama siku za Nuhu.
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuja, itakuwa kama ilivyokuwa wakati wa Nuhu.

vi.L: Vì những ngày của Nô-ê thế nào, thì sự đến của Con Người cũng sẽ như vậy.
vi.B: Sự đến của Con Người sẽ giống như những ngày của Nô-ê.
vi.R: Khi Con Người đến, mọi việc sẽ giống như vào thời của Nô-ê.

ko.L: 노아의 날들이 [그러했던] 것처럼, 인자의 오심도 그러할 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 인자가 오는 것은 노아의 때와 같을 것이다.
ko.R: 인자가 올 때에는 노아가 살던 때와 똑같을 것이다.

am.L: የኖኅ ቀኖች እንደ [ነበሩ]፣ የሰው ልጅ መምጣትም እንዲሁ ይሆናልና።
am.B: የሰው ልጅ መምጣት የኖኅን ዘመን ይመስላል።
am.R: የሰው ልጅ ሲመጣ በኖኅ ዘመን እንደ ሆነው ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: the days of Noah: the time before the flood, Genesis 6-7
decisions.reason: The next verses say what Jesus means: people went on with ordinary life and did not see the judgment coming.

decisions.choice: coming: as in 24:3 and 24:27
decisions.reason: The same word for the arrival of the Son of Man.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, used through Matthew ("Adamu" also means humankind). "Mwana wa Mtu" is closer to the Greek words; a reviewer should weigh it.

decisions.choice: "Nô-ê"
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of Noah's name, as the style guide's tradition settles for names.

decisions.choice: [그러했던] (L)
decisions.reason: Korean needs a verb for the comparison the Greek leaves without one; Literal brackets it.

source.text: ὡς γὰρ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταῖς πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες, γαμοῦντες καὶ γαμίζοντες, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ἕως ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἦρεν ἅπαντας, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: As for they were in the days the before the flood eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until which day entered Noah into the ark, \v 39 and not they knew until came the flood and took away all, so will be also the coming of the Son of the Man.

en.L: For as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, \v 39 and they did not know until the flood came and took them all away, so also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
en.B: Before the flood, people carried on with their meals and their drinking, with weddings for themselves and their children, right up to the day Noah went into the ark. \v 39 They had no idea what was coming until the flood came and swept every one of them away. The coming of the Son of Man will be like that too.
en.R: Before the great flood, people were eating and drinking. They were getting married and giving their children to be married. They kept on doing this until the day Noah went into the big boat. \v 39 They did not know what was going to happen until the flood came and carried them all away. It will be the same when the Son of Man comes.

es.L: Porque como en los días antes del diluvio estaban comiendo y bebiendo, casándose y dando en casamiento, hasta el día en que Noé entró en el arca, \v 39 y no se dieron cuenta hasta que vino el diluvio y se los llevó a todos, así será también la venida del Hijo del Hombre.
es.B: Antes del diluvio, la gente seguía comiendo y bebiendo, celebrando bodas para sí y para sus hijos, hasta el mismo día en que Noé entró en el arca. \v 39 No tenían idea de lo que venía, hasta que llegó el diluvio y los arrastró a todos. Así será también la venida del Hijo del Hombre.
es.R: Antes del gran diluvio, la gente comía y bebía. Se casaban y casaban a sus hijos. Siguieron así hasta el día en que Noé entró en la gran barca. \v 39 No sabían lo que iba a pasar, hasta que llegó el diluvio y se los llevó a todos. Lo mismo sucederá cuando venga el Hijo del Hombre.

fr.L: Car, comme dans les jours qui précédaient le déluge ils mangeaient et buvaient, se mariaient et donnaient en mariage, jusqu’au jour où Noé est entré dans l’arche, \v 39 et ils n’ont rien su jusqu’à ce que le déluge vienne et les emporte tous, ainsi sera aussi la venue du Fils de l’homme.
fr.B: Avant le déluge, les gens continuaient à manger et à boire, à se marier et à marier leurs enfants, jusqu’au jour même où Noé est entré dans l’arche. \v 39 Ils ne se doutaient de rien jusqu’à ce que le déluge arrive et les emporte tous. Il en sera de même à la venue du Fils de l’homme.
fr.R: Avant le grand déluge, les gens mangeaient et buvaient. Ils se mariaient et mariaient leurs enfants. Ils ont continué ainsi jusqu’au jour où Noé est entré dans le grand bateau. \v 39 Ils ne savaient pas ce qui allait arriver, jusqu’au moment où le déluge est venu et les a tous emportés. Ce sera la même chose quand le Fils de l’homme viendra.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa kama walivyokuwa, katika siku zile zilizotangulia gharika, wakila na kunywa, wakioa na kuoza, mpaka siku ambayo Nuhu aliingia ndani ya safina, \v 39 na hawakufahamu mpaka gharika ilipofika na kuwazoa wote, vivyo hivyo kutakuwa pia kuja kwa Mwana wa Adamu.
sw.B: Kabla ya gharika, watu waliendelea kula na kunywa, kuoa na kuwaoza watoto wao, mpaka siku ile Nuhu alipoingia katika safina. \v 39 Hawakujua lililokuwa likija mpaka gharika ilipofika, ikawazoa wote. Kuja kwa Mwana wa Adamu kutakuwa vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Kabla ya gharika kubwa, watu walikuwa wakila na kunywa. Walikuwa wakioa na kuwaoza watoto wao. Waliendelea hivyo mpaka siku ambayo Nuhu aliingia ndani ya ile mashua kubwa. \v 39 Hawakujua kitakachotokea mpaka gharika ilipokuja na kuwachukua wote. Ndivyo itakavyokuwa Mwana wa Adamu atakapokuja.

vi.L: Vì như trong những ngày trước cơn nước lụt, người ta ăn và uống, cưới vợ và gả chồng, cho đến ngày Nô-ê vào tàu, \v 39 và họ không biết gì cho đến khi nước lụt đến và cuốn đi hết thảy, thì sự đến của Con Người cũng sẽ như vậy.
vi.B: Trước cơn nước lụt, người ta vẫn ăn uống, cưới vợ, gả chồng, cho đến ngày Nô-ê vào tàu. \v 39 Họ không hề biết điều gì sắp xảy ra, cho đến khi nước lụt đến và cuốn hết thảy họ đi. Sự đến của Con Người cũng sẽ như vậy.
vi.R: Trước trận lụt lớn, người ta vẫn ăn uống. Họ vẫn lấy vợ lấy chồng và dựng vợ gả chồng cho con cái. Họ cứ sống như vậy cho đến ngày Nô-ê vào chiếc tàu lớn. \v 39 Họ không biết điều gì sắp xảy ra cho đến khi nước lụt đến và cuốn trôi tất cả họ. Khi Con Người đến, mọi việc cũng sẽ như vậy.

ko.L: 홍수 전 그 날들에 사람들이 노아가 방주에 들어간 날까지 먹고 마시며, 장가가고 시집보내고 있었고, \v 39 홍수가 나서 그들을 모두 쓸어 갈 때까지 알지 못했던 것처럼, 인자의 오심도 그러할 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 홍수가 나기 전에 사람들은 노아가 방주에 들어가던 날까지 먹고 마시고, 장가가고 시집가며 지냈다. \v 39 그들은 홍수가 나서 그들을 모두 휩쓸어 갈 때까지 무슨 일이 닥칠지 알지 못했다. 인자가 올 때에도 그와 같을 것이다.
ko.R: 큰 홍수가 나기 전에 사람들은 먹고 마시며 지냈다. 결혼도 하고 자녀들을 결혼시키기도 했다. 노아가 큰 배에 들어가던 날까지 그렇게 살았다. \v 39 그들은 홍수가 나서 모두 휩쓸려 갈 때까지 무슨 일이 일어날지 몰랐다. 인자가 올 때에도 그와 똑같을 것이다.

am.L: ከጥፋት ውኃ በፊት በነበሩት ቀኖች ኖኅ ወደ መርከብ እስከ ገባበት ቀን ድረስ ይበሉና ይጠጡ፣ ያገቡና ይድሩ ነበርና፤ \v 39 የጥፋት ውኃ መጥቶ ሁሉንም እስኪወስዳቸው ድረስም አላወቁም፤ የሰው ልጅ መምጣትም እንዲሁ ይሆናል።
am.B: ከጥፋት ውኃ በፊት ሰዎች ኖኅ ወደ መርከቡ እስከ ገባበት ቀን ድረስ ይበሉና ይጠጡ ነበር፤ ራሳቸውም ያገቡ፣ ልጆቻቸውንም ይድሩ ነበር። \v 39 የጥፋት ውኃ መጥቶ ሁሉንም ጠራርጎ እስኪወስዳቸው ድረስ የሚመጣውን ነገር አላወቁም። የሰው ልጅ መምጣትም እንደዚሁ ይሆናል።
am.R: ከታላቁ የጥፋት ውኃ በፊት ሰዎች ይበሉና ይጠጡ ነበር። ያገቡ ነበር፤ ልጆቻቸውንም ይድሩ ነበር። ኖኅ ወደ ትልቁ መርከብ እስከ ገባበት ቀን ድረስ ይህን ማድረጋቸውን ቀጠሉ። \v 39 የጥፋት ውኃ መጥቶ ሁሉንም እስኪወስዳቸው ድረስ ምን እንደሚሆን አላወቁም። የሰው ልጅ ሲመጣም እንዲሁ ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: Noah entered the ark, the flood took them away: Genesis 7:7-23
decisions.reason: Noah went into the ark and the flood came and wiped out everyone outside it.

decisions.choice: eating, drinking, marrying, giving in marriage: ordinary daily life
decisions.reason: Men married, and fathers gave their daughters in marriage. Jesus does not name any sin here. The danger is that people went on as usual, unaware.

decisions.choice: they did not know: they were unaware of what was coming
decisions.reason: The point is not that no warning was given but that they paid no attention until it was too late.

decisions.choice: weddings for themselves and their children (B); giving their children to be married (R); what was coming (B, R)
alternatives: marrying and giving in marriage; they did not know
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who gave in marriage and what they did not know.

decisions.choice: big boat
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ark was.

decisions.choice: imperfect and passé composé ("est entré") at every level
alternatives: passé simple ("entra") at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: These are Jesus's words, so the story of Noah is told in the tenses of speech, as the style guide asks for stories told inside speech and as in Luke 17:27.

decisions.choice: kuoza (to give in marriage)
decisions.reason: Swahili has its own verb for giving a child in marriage, "kuoza", beside "kuoa" (to marry a wife), so the Greek pair comes through as a pair (meaning decision m2). "Kuolewa" (to be married, of a woman) would change the second verb's meaning.

decisions.choice: "cơn nước lụt" (L, B), "trận lụt lớn" (R); "tàu" (L, B), "chiếc tàu lớn" (R) for the ark
decisions.reason: "Tàu" is the word Vietnamese Bibles use for Noah's ark, and it means a large boat in plain speech; "cưới vợ và gả chồng" says marrying and giving in marriage with the everyday pair of verbs.

decisions.choice: "장가가고 시집보내다" (L); "장가가고 시집가다" (B); "결혼도 하고 자녀들을 결혼시키다" (R); "방주" (L, B), "큰 배" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean has paired verbs for marrying and giving in marriage; Balanced uses the familiar pair, Readable says it plainly as the English Readable does. "방주" is the established word for the ark; Readable says "big boat" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "노아가 방주에 들어간 날까지" placed before the verbs (L)
decisions.reason: Korean puts the limit before the verbs it limits; the content of each verse stays after its marker.

decisions.choice: "for as ... so" given as a statement about the days before the flood, with "so will be the coming" as its own clause in verse 39
alternatives: one Amharic sentence with "እንደ ነበሩ ... እንዲሁ" spanning both verses
decisions.reason: An Amharic comparison of this length would put the verbs of verse 38 after the material of verse 39. Splitting it keeps each verse's content after its own marker.

source.text: τότε δύο ἔσονται ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, εἷς παραλαμβάνεται καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται·

records.literal_gloss: Then two will be in the field, one is taken and one is left;

en.L: Then two will be in the field; one is taken and one is left.
en.B: Two people will then be working in the field: one is taken, and the other is left.
en.R: At that time two people will be working in a field. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.

es.L: Entonces dos estarán en el campo; uno es tomado y uno es dejado.
es.B: Entonces habrá dos personas trabajando en el campo: una es llevada y la otra es dejada.
es.R: En ese momento, dos personas estarán trabajando en un campo. Una será llevada, y la otra será dejada atrás.

fr.L: Alors deux seront dans le champ : l’un est pris et l’autre est laissé.
fr.B: Deux personnes travailleront alors dans les champs : l’une est prise, et l’autre laissée.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, deux personnes seront en train de travailler dans un champ. L’une sera prise, et l’autre sera laissée.

sw.L: Wakati huo wawili watakuwa shambani; mmoja anachukuliwa na mmoja anaachwa.
sw.B: Wakati huo watu wawili watakuwa wakifanya kazi shambani: mmoja anachukuliwa, na mwingine anaachwa.
sw.R: Wakati huo watu wawili watakuwa wakifanya kazi shambani. Mmoja atachukuliwa, na mwingine ataachwa.

vi.L: Bấy giờ hai người sẽ ở ngoài đồng; một người được đem đi và một người bị để lại.
vi.B: Lúc ấy, hai người đang làm việc ngoài đồng: một người được đem đi, còn người kia bị để lại.
vi.R: Lúc ấy, hai người đang làm việc ngoài đồng. Một người sẽ được đem đi, còn người kia sẽ bị bỏ lại.

ko.L: 그때에 두 사람이 밭에 있을 것인데, 하나는 데려가지고 하나는 남겨진다.
ko.B: 그때에 두 사람이 밭에서 일하고 있으면, 한 사람은 데려가고 다른 한 사람은 남겨 둘 것이다.
ko.R: 그때 두 사람이 밭에서 일하고 있을 것이다. 한 사람은 데려가고, 다른 사람은 남겨질 것이다.

am.L: ያን ጊዜ ሁለት [ሰዎች] በእርሻ ውስጥ ይሆናሉ፤ አንዱ ይወሰዳል፣ አንዱም ይተዋል።
am.B: በዚያን ጊዜ ሁለት ሰዎች በእርሻ ውስጥ ይሠራሉ፤ አንዱ ይወሰዳል፣ ሌላው ይተዋል።
am.R: በዚያን ጊዜ ሁለት ሰዎች በአንድ እርሻ ውስጥ ይሠራሉ። አንዱ ይወሰዳል፤ ሌላው ወደ ኋላ ይቀራል።

decisions.choice: taken, left: taken to be with the Son of Man, or left for judgment
alternatives: taken away in judgment, as by the flood, and left to live
decisions.reason: The verb "taken" is used of taking someone along as a companion (1:20; 17:1), and the angels gather the chosen in 24:31. But the flood "took" people away in judgment (24:39), so some read the one taken as judged. The verse stresses the sudden separation more than which is which.

decisions.choice: is taken, is left: present tense of a future event
decisions.reason: The present makes the scene vivid. It will happen then.

decisions.choice: two people ... working
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "two". Balanced and Readable say they are people at work; the next verse speaks of women, so this one is not limited to men.

decisions.choice: "được đem đi" and "bị để lại"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks a passive as good ("được") or bad ("bị"); the meaning decision reads being taken as being taken to the Son of Man and being left as being left for judgment, so "được" goes with the first and "bị" with the second. The same in 24:41.

decisions.choice: "데려가지고 ... 남겨진다" (L), present passives
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present passive for the future event (meaning decision). Balanced uses active verbs with no named subject, which Korean prefers, and leaves who takes them unsaid, as the Greek does.

source.text: δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐν τῷ μύλῳ, μία παραλαμβάνεται καὶ μία ἀφίεται.

records.literal_gloss: two grinding at the mill, one is taken and one is left.

en.L: Two [women will be] grinding at the mill; one is taken and one is left.
en.B: Two women will be grinding grain at the mill: one is taken, and the other is left.
en.R: Two women will be grinding grain with a millstone. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.

es.L: Dos [mujeres estarán] moliendo en el molino; una es tomada y una es dejada.
es.B: Dos mujeres estarán moliendo grano en el molino: una es llevada y la otra es dejada.
es.R: Dos mujeres estarán moliendo grano con una piedra de moler. Una será llevada, y la otra será dejada atrás.

fr.L: Deux [femmes] moudront à la meule : l’une est prise et l’autre est laissée.
fr.B: Deux femmes moudront du grain à la meule : l’une est prise, et l’autre laissée.
fr.R: Deux femmes seront en train de moudre du grain avec une meule. L’une sera prise, et l’autre sera laissée.

sw.L: [Wanawake] wawili [watakuwa] wakisaga kwenye jiwe la kusagia; mmoja anachukuliwa na mmoja anaachwa.
sw.B: Wanawake wawili watakuwa wakisaga nafaka kwenye jiwe la kusagia: mmoja anachukuliwa, na mwingine anaachwa.
sw.R: Wanawake wawili watakuwa wakisaga nafaka kwa jiwe la kusagia. Mmoja atachukuliwa, na mwingine ataachwa.

vi.L: Hai [người phụ nữ] đang xay cối; một người được đem đi và một người bị để lại.
vi.B: Hai người phụ nữ đang xay bột tại cối xay: một người được đem đi, còn người kia bị để lại.
vi.R: Hai người phụ nữ đang dùng cối đá xay bột. Một người sẽ được đem đi, còn người kia sẽ bị bỏ lại.

ko.L: 두 [여자가] 맷돌을 갈고 있을 것인데, 하나는 데려가지고 하나는 남겨진다.
ko.B: 두 여자가 맷돌질을 하고 있으면, 한 사람은 데려가고 다른 한 사람은 남겨 둘 것이다.
ko.R: 두 여자가 맷돌로 곡식을 갈고 있을 것이다. 한 사람은 데려가고, 다른 사람은 남겨질 것이다.

am.L: ሁለት [ሴቶች] በወፍጮ ይፈጫሉ፤ አንዲቱ ትወሰዳለች፣ አንዲቱም ትተዋለች።
am.B: ሁለት ሴቶች በወፍጮ እህል ይፈጫሉ፤ አንዲቱ ትወሰዳለች፣ ሌላይቱ ትተዋለች።
am.R: ሁለት ሴቶች በወፍጮ ድንጋይ እህል ይፈጫሉ። አንዲቱ ትወሰዳለች፤ ሌላይቱ ወደ ኋላ ትቀራለች።

decisions.choice: grinding at the mill: grinding grain into flour, women's daily work at home
alternatives: a large mill run by animals
decisions.reason: Grain was ground by hand each day with a pair of stones. The Greek forms show that the two are women.

decisions.choice: women (L in brackets; B, R); grain (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek words are feminine, so every level says women. Balanced and Readable say what was ground.

decisions.choice: [Wanawake] (L); Wanawake (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek shows that the two are women only by the endings of its words (meaning decision m1). "Wawili" and "mmoja" do not show it in Swahili, so the word for women is supplied, in brackets at Literal, as in English.

decisions.choice: [여자가] (L); "여자" (B, R); "맷돌" for the mill
decisions.reason: The Greek participles are feminine; Korean shows this with the noun, which Literal brackets. "맷돌" is the Korean hand mill, the household tool meant here (meaning decision).

source.text: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Keep awake therefore, because not you know on what day the Lord of you comes.

en.L: Keep watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
en.B: So stay alert, since you do not know which day your Lord will come.
en.R: So keep watching and be ready! You do not know what day your Lord will come.

es.L: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} en vela, pues, porque no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} en qué día viene {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Señor.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} alerta, pues no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} qué día vendrá {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Señor.
es.R: Por eso, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} atentos y {{plural_you:prepárense|preparaos}}. No {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} qué día vendrá {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Señor.

fr.L: Veillez donc, car vous ne savez pas quel jour votre Seigneur vient.
fr.B: Restez donc vigilants, puisque vous ne savez pas quel jour votre Seigneur viendra.
fr.R: Alors restez éveillés et soyez prêts ! Vous ne savez pas quel jour votre Seigneur viendra.

sw.L: Basi kesheni, kwa sababu hamjui ni siku ipi Bwana wenu anakuja.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo kaeni macho, kwa kuwa hamjui ni siku gani Bwana wenu atakuja.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo endeleeni kukesha na kuwa tayari! Hamjui ni siku gani Bwana wenu atakuja.

vi.L: Vậy hãy thức canh, vì các con không biết ngày nào Chúa của các con đến.
vi.B: Vậy hãy luôn tỉnh thức, vì các con không biết ngày nào Chúa của các con sẽ đến.
vi.R: Vậy hãy thức canh và sẵn sàng! Các con không biết ngày nào Chúa của các con sẽ đến.

ko.L: 그러므로 깨어 있어라. 너희의 주가 어느 날에 오는지 너희가 알지 못하기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 깨어 있어라. 너희 주가 어느 날에 올지 너희는 모른다.
ko.R: 그러니 잠들지 말고 깨어 있어라! 너희 주가 어느 날에 올지 너희는 모른다.

am.L: እንግዲህ ትጉ፤ ጌታችሁ በየትኛው ቀን እንደሚመጣ አታውቁምና።
am.B: ስለዚህ ነቅታችሁ ጠብቁ፤ ጌታችሁ የሚመጣበትን ቀን አታውቁምና።
am.R: ስለዚህ ተጠባበቁ፤ ተዘጋጁም! ጌታችሁ በየትኛው ቀን እንደሚመጣ አታውቁም።

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay awake. Here it means to be ready for the Lord's coming. It returns in 24:43, 25:13 and at Gethsemane (26:38-41).

decisions.choice: your Lord: Jesus, the Son of Man whose coming is described
decisions.reason: The verses around speak of the coming of the Son of Man (24:39, 44). He is the disciples' Lord.

decisions.choice: on what day, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: at what hour, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "hour", as in 24:44. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: stay alert (B); keep watching and be ready (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what keeping awake means here.

decisions.choice: Veillez (L); Restez vigilants (B); Restez éveillés et soyez prêts (R); the same in 25:13
decisions.reason: As in Mark 13:33-37, "veiller" is kept for this verb, keep awake, and "Prenez garde" for the verb "see" in 24:4.

decisions.choice: "thức canh" (L, R), "luôn tỉnh thức" (B); "Chúa của các con"
decisions.reason: "Thức canh" is the word for this verb in Mark 13:34-37, joining staying awake and keeping guard; the same in 24:43, 25:13 and Gethsemane. "Chúa" is Jesus, the coming Son of Man (meaning decision), so it is capitalised and has no setting.

decisions.choice: "깨어 있어라" for gregoreo, every level, through Matthew 24-25; Readable adds "잠들지 말고"
decisions.reason: The phrase of the Korean Mark 13:33-37, which ties Jesus' call to watch to Gethsemane (26:38-41).

decisions.choice: "너희의 주" (L), "너희 주" (B, R), with no honorific ("오는지", "올지")
decisions.reason: The Lord is Jesus himself (meaning decision); he speaks of himself, so Korean gives no honorific, as with "인자". "주" rather than "주인" keeps the title.

decisions.choice: "ትጉ" (keep watch, L); "ነቅታችሁ ጠብቁ" (stay awake and watch, B); "ተጠባበቁ፤ ተዘጋጁም" (keep watching and be ready, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a present command to keep awake and alert, not to wake from sleep, so Literal uses "ትጉ" (be vigilant) and the other levels spell out watching.

source.text: ἐκεῖνο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ φυλακῇ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ἐγρηγόρησεν ἂν καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴασεν διορυχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: That but know that if had known the master of the house in what watch the thief comes, he would have kept awake and not would have allowed to be dug through the house of him.

en.L: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be dug through.
en.B: Think about this. A homeowner who knew at what time of night a thief was coming would stay awake and not allow anyone to dig through the walls of his house.
en.R: Think about this. Suppose the owner of a house knew what time of night a robber would come. He would stay awake. He would not let the robber break into his house.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} esto: que si el dueño de casa hubiera sabido en qué vigilia viene el ladrón, habría vigilado y no habría permitido que su casa fuera horadada.
es.B: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en esto: el dueño de una casa que supiera a qué hora de la noche va a venir el ladrón se quedaría despierto y no dejaría que nadie abriera un boquete en las paredes de su casa.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en esto. Supongamos que el dueño de una casa supiera a qué hora de la noche va a llegar un ladrón. Se quedaría despierto. No dejaría que el ladrón entrara a la fuerza en su casa.

fr.L: Mais sachez ceci : si le maître de maison avait su à quelle veille le voleur venait, il aurait veillé et n’aurait pas laissé percer sa maison.
fr.B: Réfléchissez à ceci. Un propriétaire qui saurait à quelle heure de la nuit un voleur doit venir resterait éveillé et ne laisserait personne percer les murs de sa maison.
fr.R: Réfléchissez bien. Imaginez que le propriétaire d’une maison sache à quelle heure de la nuit un voleur va venir. Il resterait éveillé. Il ne laisserait pas le voleur entrer de force chez lui.

sw.L: Lakini jueni jambo hili, kwamba kama mwenye nyumba angalifahamu ni lindo lipi [la usiku] mwizi anakuja, angalikaa macho, wala asingaliruhusu nyumba yake itobolewe.
sw.B: Fikirini jambo hili. Mwenye nyumba ambaye angejua ni saa ngapi za usiku mwizi angekuja, angekaa macho, wala asingemwacha mtu yeyote atoboe ukuta wa nyumba yake.
sw.R: Fikirini jambo hili. Tuseme mwenye nyumba angejua ni saa ngapi usiku mwizi atakuja. Angekaa macho. Asingemwacha mwizi avunje na kuingia nyumbani mwake.

vi.L: Nhưng hãy biết điều này: nếu chủ nhà biết vào canh nào kẻ trộm đến, thì ông ấy đã thức canh và không để nhà mình bị khoét vách.
vi.B: Hãy nghĩ điều này: nếu chủ nhà biết vào giờ nào ban đêm kẻ trộm sẽ đến, thì ông ấy đã thức canh, không để kẻ trộm khoét vách vào nhà mình.
vi.R: Hãy suy nghĩ điều này. Giả sử chủ nhà biết vào giờ nào ban đêm kẻ trộm sẽ đến. Ông ấy sẽ thức để canh. Ông ấy sẽ không để kẻ trộm phá vách vào nhà mình.

ko.L: 그러나 이것을 알아라. 집주인이 도둑이 밤 몇 경에 오는지 알았더라면, 그는 깨어 있어서 자기 집이 뚫리도록 내버려 두지 않았을 것이다.
ko.B: 이것을 생각해 보아라. 도둑이 밤 몇 시에 올지 집주인이 알았다면, 그는 깨어 있어서 도둑이 벽을 뚫고 집에 들어오지 못하게 했을 것이다.
ko.R: 이것을 생각해 보아라. 집주인이 도둑이 밤 몇 시에 올지 안다고 하자. 그러면 그는 잠들지 않고 깨어 있을 것이다. 도둑이 자기 집에 들어오지 못하게 할 것이다.

am.L: ይህን ግን እወቁ፤ የቤቱ ባለቤት ሌባው በየትኛው ክፍለ ሌሊት እንደሚመጣ ቢያውቅ ኖሮ በነቃ ነበር፤ ቤቱም እንዲቆፈር ባልፈቀደ ነበር።
am.B: ይህን አስቡት፤ የቤት ባለቤት ሌባ በሌሊቱ በየትኛው ሰዓት እንደሚመጣ ቢያውቅ ነቅቶ ይጠብቅ ነበር፤ ማንም የቤቱን ግድግዳ ቆፍሮ እንዲገባ አይፈቅድም ነበር።
am.R: ይህን አስቡት። የአንድ ቤት ባለቤት ሌባ በሌሊት በየትኛው ሰዓት እንደሚመጣ ቢያውቅ ኖሮ ነቅቶ ይጠብቅ ነበር። ሌባው ቤቱን ሰብሮ እንዲገባ አይፈቅድለትም ነበር።

decisions.choice: watch: a part of the night
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, four in the Roman reckoning (14:25). A thief comes at night, at a time no one expects.

decisions.choice: be dug through: broken into through the wall
decisions.reason: Many houses had walls of mud brick, which a thief could dig through (6:19).

decisions.choice: the thief: a picture of an arrival no one expects
alternatives: a picture of the Son of Man's character
decisions.reason: Only the timing is compared. The same picture is used of the day of the Lord in 1 Thessalonians 5:2.

decisions.choice: Think about this, then the example told as a fact (B) or a supposition (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the contrary-to-fact sentence into a plain example.

decisions.choice: itobolewe (be bored through, L); atoboe ukuta (dig through the wall, B)
decisions.reason: A thief broke into a house by digging through its wall (meaning decision m2). "Kutoboa" says that, as it would of a mud-walled house today; "kuvunjwa" (be broken into) loses the picture. Readable says "avunje na kuingia", as the English Readable says "break into".

decisions.choice: "canh" (L), "giờ nào ban đêm" (B, R); "khoét vách" (L, B), "phá vách" (R)
decisions.reason: A watch is one part of the night (meaning decision); Vietnamese "canh" names the same old division, which Balanced and Readable say as a time of night. Houses were broken into through the wall, and "khoét vách" is the Vietnamese for that very act.

decisions.choice: "밤 몇 경" (L); "밤 몇 시" (B, R) for phylake
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches (meaning decision); Literal keeps the old word "경" for a night watch, Balanced and Readable give the plain time.

decisions.choice: "뚫리다" (L); "벽을 뚫다" (B)
decisions.reason: Thieves dug through the mud-brick walls (meaning decision); Balanced names the wall.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὥρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this also you be ready, because in which not you think hour the Son of the Man comes.

en.L: Because of this you also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
en.B: So you too must stay prepared: the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not imagine.
en.R: So you must always be ready too. The Son of Man will come at a time when you do not think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come.

es.L: Por esto también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:estén|estad}} preparados, porque a la hora que no {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} viene el Hijo del Hombre.
es.B: Así que también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} estar preparados: el Hijo del Hombre viene a una hora que no {{plural_you:se imaginan|os imagináis}}.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} estar siempre listos. El Hijo del Hombre vendrá a una hora en que no {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que vaya a venir.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi vous aussi, soyez prêts, car c’est à une heure que vous ne pensez pas que le Fils de l’homme vient.
fr.B: Vous aussi, tenez-vous donc prêts : le Fils de l’homme vient à une heure que vous n’imaginez pas.
fr.R: Alors vous aussi, soyez toujours prêts. Le Fils de l’homme viendra au moment où vous ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}attendrez pas.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo nanyi pia iweni tayari, kwa kuwa katika saa msiyoifikiri Mwana wa Adamu anakuja.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ninyi pia muwe tayari, kwa maana Mwana wa Adamu anakuja saa msiyoitazamia.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ninyi pia muwe tayari wakati wote. Mwana wa Adamu atakuja wakati ambao hamfikiri kwamba atakuja.

vi.L: Vì thế, các con cũng phải sẵn sàng, vì Con Người đến vào giờ các con không ngờ.
vi.B: Vậy các con cũng phải luôn sẵn sàng, vì Con Người sẽ đến vào giờ các con không ngờ tới.
vi.R: Vậy các con cũng phải luôn luôn sẵn sàng. Con Người sẽ đến vào lúc các con không nghĩ là Con Người sẽ đến.

ko.L: 그러므로 너희도 준비되어 있어라. 너희가 생각하지 않은 때에 인자가 오기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러니 너희도 늘 준비하고 있어라. 인자는 너희가 생각하지도 못한 때에 올 것이다.
ko.R: 그러니 너희도 언제나 준비하고 있어라. 인자는 너희가 생각하지 않은 때에 올 것이다.

am.L: ስለዚህ እናንተም ዝግጁዎች ሁኑ፤ የሰው ልጅ ይመጣል ብላችሁ በማትገምቱት ሰዓት ይመጣልና።
am.B: ስለዚህ እናንተም ተዘጋጁ፤ የሰው ልጅ ፈጽሞ ባልገመታችሁት ሰዓት ይመጣልና።
am.R: ስለዚህ እናንተም ሁልጊዜ ዝግጁ ሁኑ። የሰው ልጅ ይመጣል ብላችሁ በማታስቡበት ጊዜ ይመጣል።

decisions.choice: be ready: a present command, keep on being ready
decisions.reason: Since the hour is unknown, readiness must last.

decisions.choice: is coming: a present tense of something certain to happen
alternatives: he is on his way now
decisions.reason: The present tense makes the coming sure, as in 24:42-43.

decisions.choice: always
decisions.reason: Readable shows the force of the present command, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "Con Người" repeated (R), where the English has "he" with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of Man; repeating the title avoids making him call himself "Ngài", as in Mark 13:27.

decisions.choice: "오기 때문이다" (L), present tense
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present for an event certain to happen (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable use the future. "때" for hora, as in the Korean John.

source.text: Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς δοῦλος καὶ φρόνιμος ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκετείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν τροφὴν ἐν καιρῷ;

records.literal_gloss: Who then is the faithful slave and wise whom set the master over the household of him to give to them the food in season?

en.L: Who then is the faithful and wise slave whom the master set over his household to give them the food in season?
en.B: Who, then, is the servant that is trustworthy and sensible, whom the master has put in charge of his household staff to give them their food when it is due?
en.R: Who is the servant who is faithful and wise? Suppose a master puts one of his servants in charge of the other servants in his house. That servant must give them their food at the right time.

es.L: ¿Quién es, pues, el esclavo fiel y prudente a quien el señor puso sobre su servidumbre para darles el alimento a su tiempo?
es.B: ¿Quién es, entonces, el siervo digno de confianza y sensato a quien el señor ha puesto al frente de los criados de su casa, para que les dé la comida a su debido tiempo?
es.R: ¿Quién es el siervo fiel y sabio? Supongamos que un hombre pone a uno de sus siervos a cargo de los otros siervos de su casa. Ese siervo tiene que darles la comida a la hora debida.

fr.L: Qui donc est l’esclave fidèle et avisé que le maître a établi sur les gens de sa maison pour leur donner la nourriture en temps voulu ?
fr.B: Qui donc est le serviteur digne de confiance et sensé que le maître a chargé des domestiques de sa maison, pour leur donner leur nourriture au moment voulu ?
fr.R: Qui est le serviteur fidèle et sage ? Imaginez qu’un maître charge un de ses serviteurs de s’occuper des autres serviteurs de sa maison. Ce serviteur doit leur donner leur nourriture au bon moment.

sw.L: Basi ni nani yule mtumwa mwaminifu na mwenye busara, ambaye bwana [wake] alimweka juu ya watu wa nyumba yake ili awape chakula kwa majira yake?
sw.B: Basi ni nani mtumishi anayeaminika na mwenye busara, ambaye bwana wake amemweka kusimamia watumishi wa nyumba yake, ili awape chakula chao wakati unaofaa?
sw.R: Ni nani mtumishi mwaminifu na mwenye hekima? Tuseme bwana mmoja anamweka mmoja wa watumishi wake kuwasimamia watumishi wengine wa nyumbani mwake. Mtumishi huyo anapaswa kuwapa chakula chao kwa wakati unaofaa.

vi.L: Vậy ai là nô lệ trung tín và khôn ngoan mà chủ đã đặt coi sóc người nhà của mình, để cho họ đồ ăn đúng giờ?
vi.B: Vậy ai là người đầy tớ trung tín và khôn ngoan, được chủ giao cho cai quản những người giúp việc trong nhà, để phát lương thực cho họ đúng lúc?
vi.R: Ai là người đầy tớ trung tín và khôn ngoan? Giả sử một ông chủ giao cho một đầy tớ trông coi các đầy tớ khác trong nhà mình. Người đầy tớ ấy phải phát đồ ăn cho họ đúng lúc.

ko.L: 그렇다면 주인이 자기 집안 [종들] 위에 세워 제때에 그들에게 양식을 나누어 주게 한, 신실하고 지혜로운 종은 누구냐?
ko.B: 그렇다면 주인이 자기 집안 종들을 맡겨 제때에 양식을 나누어 주게 한, 믿음직하고 슬기로운 종은 누구겠느냐?
ko.R: 누가 신실하고 지혜로운 종이겠느냐? 어떤 주인이 자기 종 하나에게 집안의 다른 종들을 맡겼다고 하자. 그 종은 제때에 다른 종들에게 먹을 것을 나누어 주어야 한다.

am.L: እንግዲያ ታማኙና አስተዋዩ ባሪያ፣ ምግባቸውን በወቅቱ እንዲሰጣቸው ጌታው በቤቱ አገልጋዮች ላይ የሾመው፣ ማን ነው?
am.B: ታዲያ ጌታው በቤቱ አገልጋዮች ላይ ኃላፊ አድርጎ የሾመውና ምግባቸውን በሰዓቱ የሚሰጣቸው፣ ታማኝና አስተዋይ አገልጋይ ማን ነው?
am.R: ታማኝና ጥበበኛ የሆነው አገልጋይ ማን ነው? አንድ ጌታ ከአገልጋዮቹ አንዱን በቤቱ ባሉት ሌሎች አገልጋዮች ላይ ኃላፊ አደረገው እንበል። ያ አገልጋይ በተገቢው ጊዜ ምግባቸውን ሊሰጣቸው ይገባል።

decisions.choice: who then is: a question that invites the hearers to see themselves as the slave
decisions.reason: The question is answered in 24:46: the faithful slave is the one the master finds doing his work. The disciples are to be that slave.

decisions.choice: slave, household: a trusted slave put over the other household slaves
decisions.reason: In large households a slave could be put in charge of the others, with the care of food and supplies. The word for slave is the same as in 10:24.

decisions.choice: faithful and wise: trustworthy, and sensible in doing what the time requires
decisions.reason: "Faithful" here means reliable. "Wise" is the word used of the man who built on rock (7:24).

decisions.choice: in season: at the proper time
alternatives: in a certain season of the year
decisions.reason: The phrase means at the right time, when the food is due.

decisions.choice: master, his, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, though the picture points to Jesus. The word is the same as "Lord" in 24:42.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: trustworthy and sensible
decisions.reason: Balanced uses everyday words for the two qualities, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: esclavo (L); siervo (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek word is a slave (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "siervo", since the parable is about faithful service, not slavery itself. The book-wide choice; the same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: señor, lowercase, at every level, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no setting, as in English. Lowercase "señor" is the master of servants and is the same word as "Señor" in 24:42, as the Greek uses one word for both. The same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R); le maître, with no deity_pronoun span (for 24:45-51 and the parables of chapter 25)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as the English and as in Luke 12:42-47. "Maître" is the French word for a slave's owner; "seigneur" would sound feudal. The master is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek word is a slave (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", since the parable is about faithful service, not slavery itself. The book-wide choice; the same through 24:51.

decisions.choice: bwana, lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is a figure in a parable, so he is "bwana" (master) and his pronouns take no setting, as in English. Swahili uses the same word as "Bwana" in 24:42, so the link the Greek makes comes through.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos (24:45-51); "chủ" for the master, with no setting
decisions.reason: The style guide's rendering of doulos, as in Mark 13:34. The master is a figure in a parable, so "chủ" and "ông" take no deity_pronoun span, as the English decision says.

decisions.choice: "trung tín và khôn ngoan"
alternatives: "đáng tin cậy và biết suy xét"
decisions.reason: One pair at every level, so the master's praise in 25:21-23 and the wise bridesmaids in 25:2 can echo it; the meaning decision gives the sense, trustworthy and sensible.

decisions.choice: "종" for doulos at every level; "주인" for kyrios, with no honorific, through Matthew 24:45-51
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 18:23-34: "종" already names someone owned by a master, and "주인" is the word for the master in a parable, "주님" being kept for God and Jesus. The English gives the master no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "신실하고 지혜로운" (L, R); "믿음직하고 슬기로운" (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced says trustworthy and sensible, as the English Balanced does; "충성되고" is the older word.

decisions.choice: "ባሪያ" (slave, L); "አገልጋይ" (servant, B, R); "ጌታው" (his master) at every level
decisions.reason: The parable turns on the trust given to a household slave and how he serves, so Balanced and Readable say "አገልጋይ", as the English does; Literal keeps the Greek word. "ጌታ" is the ordinary word for a master and needs no setting.

source.text: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει οὕτως ποιοῦντα·

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the slave that whom having come the master of him will find so doing;

en.L: Blessed [is] that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.
en.B: That servant will be blessed if, when his master comes, he finds him at that very work.
en.R: That servant will be blessed if his master comes back and finds him doing his job.

es.L: Dichoso aquel esclavo a quien su señor, al venir, encuentre haciendo así.
es.B: Dichoso ese siervo si, cuando llegue su señor, lo encuentra haciendo precisamente eso.
es.R: Ese siervo será dichoso si su señor regresa y lo encuentra haciendo su trabajo.

fr.L: Heureux cet esclave que son maître, à son arrivée, trouvera en train de faire ainsi.
fr.B: Heureux ce serviteur, si son maître, en arrivant, le trouve occupé à ce travail même.
fr.R: Ce serviteur sera heureux si son maître revient et le trouve en train de faire son travail.

sw.L: Heri mtumwa huyo, ambaye bwana wake akifika atamkuta anafanya hivyo.
sw.B: Heri mtumishi huyo ambaye bwana wake atakaporudi atamkuta akifanya kazi hiyo hasa.
sw.R: Mtumishi huyo amebarikiwa ikiwa bwana wake atarudi na kumkuta akifanya kazi yake.

vi.L: Phước cho nô lệ ấy là người khi chủ mình đến sẽ thấy đang làm như vậy.
vi.B: Phước cho người đầy tớ ấy nếu khi chủ về, thấy anh đang làm đúng như thế.
vi.R: Người đầy tớ ấy sẽ được phước nếu ông chủ trở về và thấy anh đang làm công việc của mình.

ko.L: 주인이 와서 그렇게 하고 있는 것을 보게 될 그 종은 복이 있다.
ko.B: 주인이 돌아와서 볼 때에 그렇게 일하고 있는 종은 복이 있다.
ko.R: 주인이 돌아왔을 때 자기 일을 잘하고 있는 종은 복이 있다.

am.L: የተባረከ [ነው] ያ ባሪያ፣ ጌታው መጥቶ እንዲህ ሲያደርግ የሚያገኘው።
am.B: ጌታው በሚመጣበት ጊዜ በዚሁ ሥራ ላይ ቢያገኘው ያ አገልጋይ የተባረከ ይሆናል።
am.R: ጌታው ተመልሶ ሲመጣ ሥራውን ሲሠራ ቢያገኘው ያ አገልጋይ የተባረከ ይሆናል።

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
decisions.reason: As in 5:3-11, the word describes someone well off in God's eyes. Here it is the slave the master rewards.

decisions.choice: so doing: giving the household their food as he was told
decisions.reason: "So" points back to the task of 24:45.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: Heureux
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes and Luke 12:43: the word for those God favors is "Heureux" in French; "béni" belongs to the other Greek word for blessing.

decisions.choice: "Phước cho" (L, B); "sẽ được phước" (R)
decisions.reason: The Beatitudes' word in the Vietnamese Matthew (5:3-11), so the blessing here is heard as the same kind of blessing.

decisions.choice: "복이 있다" for makarios
decisions.reason: The Beatitudes' word in the Korean Matthew (5:3-11).

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you that over all the possessions of him he will set him.

en.L: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all his possessions.
en.B: Truly I tell you, the master will put him in charge of everything he owns.
en.R: I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que sobre todos sus bienes lo pondrá.
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el señor lo pondrá a cargo de todo lo que tiene.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: el señor pondrá a ese siervo a cargo de todo lo que tiene.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis : il l’établira sur tous ses biens.
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : le maître le chargera de tout ce qu’il possède.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : le maître chargera ce serviteur de tout ce qu’il possède.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia kwamba juu ya mali yake yote atamweka.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, bwana wake atamweka kusimamia mali yake yote.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: bwana wake atamweka mtumishi huyo kusimamia kila kitu alicho nacho.

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con rằng chủ sẽ đặt người ấy coi sóc tất cả tài sản của mình.
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, chủ sẽ giao cho anh cai quản tất cả tài sản của mình.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con, ông chủ sẽ giao cho người đầy tớ ấy trông coi mọi thứ ông có.

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 주인은 자기 모든 재산 위에 그를 세울 것이다.
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 주인은 자기의 모든 재산을 그에게 맡길 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 주인은 그 종에게 자기가 가진 모든 것을 맡길 것이다.

am.L: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ በንብረቱ ሁሉ ላይ ይሾመዋል።
am.B: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ ጌታው ባለው ነገር ሁሉ ላይ ኃላፊ ያደርገዋል።
am.R: እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ፣ ጌታው ያን አገልጋይ ባለው ነገር ሁሉ ላይ ኃላፊ ያደርገዋል።

decisions.choice: set over all his possessions: the reward of faithful work is greater trust
decisions.reason: The faithful slave is given more to care for, as in the parable that follows (25:21, 23).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as in 24:2.

decisions.choice: the master; that servant (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is who.

decisions.choice: "주인은" at every level; "그 종에게" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean names the subject where English says "he"; Literal does not bracket it, since the Greek verb carries the subject.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ κακὸς δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει μου ὁ κύριος, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίῃ δὲ καὶ πίνῃ μετὰ τῶν μεθυόντων, ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

records.literal_gloss: If but says the evil slave that in the heart of him, Delays my the master, \v 49 and begins to beat the fellow slaves of him, eats and drinks with those being drunk, \v 50 will come the master of the slave that in day in which not he expects and in hour which not he knows, \v 51 and will cut in two him and the portion of him with the hypocrites will put; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.

en.L: But if that evil slave says in his heart, 'My master is delaying,' \v 49 and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with the drunkards, \v 50 the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect [him] and at an hour that he does not know, \v 51 and will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the hypocrites; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
en.B: But that servant may be wicked. He may think to himself, 'My master is a long time coming,' \v 49 and start to beat his fellow servants, while he eats and drinks with drunkards. \v 50 If so, his master will come on a day he does not look for, at an hour he does not know. \v 51 The master will cut him in pieces and put him with the hypocrites, where people will weep and grind their teeth.
en.R: But suppose that servant is evil. He says to himself, 'My master will not come back for a long time.' \v 49 So he begins to beat the other servants. He eats and drinks with people who get drunk. \v 50 Then the master will come back on a day when the servant does not expect him, at a time he does not know. \v 51 The master will punish him terribly and put him with the hypocrites. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

es.L: Pero si aquel esclavo malo dice en su corazón: “Mi señor tarda”, \v 49 y comienza a golpear a sus compañeros esclavos, y come y bebe con los borrachos, \v 50 vendrá el señor de aquel esclavo en un día en que no [lo] espera y a una hora que no conoce, \v 51 y lo partirá en dos y pondrá su parte con los hipócritas; allí estará el llanto y el rechinar de los dientes.
es.B: Pero puede que ese siervo sea malvado. Puede que piense: “Mi señor tarda mucho en venir”, \v 49 y comience a golpear a los demás siervos, mientras come y bebe con borrachos. \v 50 Si es así, su señor vendrá un día en que no lo espera, a una hora que no sabe. \v 51 El señor lo hará pedazos y lo pondrá con los hipócritas, donde la gente llorará y rechinará los dientes.
es.R: Pero supongamos que ese siervo es malo. Se dice a sí mismo: “Mi señor va a tardar mucho en volver”. \v 49 Entonces empieza a golpear a los otros siervos. Come y bebe con gente que se emborracha. \v 50 Entonces el señor volverá un día en que el siervo no lo espera, a una hora que no sabe. \v 51 El señor lo castigará con mucha dureza y lo pondrá con los hipócritas. Allí llorarán y rechinarán los dientes.

fr.L: Mais si ce mauvais esclave dit dans son cœur : “Mon maître tarde”, \v 49 et qu’il se mette à battre ses compagnons d’esclavage, et qu’il mange et boive avec les ivrognes, \v 50 le maître de cet esclave viendra un jour où il ne [l’]attend pas et à une heure qu’il ne connaît pas, \v 51 et il le coupera en deux et lui assignera sa part avec les hypocrites ; là il y aura les pleurs et les grincements de dents.
fr.B: Mais ce serviteur pourrait être méchant. Il pourrait se dire : “Mon maître tarde à venir”, \v 49 et se mettre à battre ses compagnons de service, tout en mangeant et en buvant avec des ivrognes. \v 50 Alors son maître arrivera un jour où il ne s’y attend pas, à une heure qu’il ne connaît pas. \v 51 Le maître le mettra en pièces et le placera avec les hypocrites, là où l’on pleurera et grincera des dents.
fr.R: Mais imaginez que ce serviteur soit méchant. Il se dit : “Mon maître ne reviendra pas avant longtemps.” \v 49 Alors il se met à frapper les autres serviteurs. Il mange et il boit avec des gens qui s’enivrent. \v 50 Alors le maître reviendra un jour où le serviteur ne l’attend pas, à un moment qu’il ne connaît pas. \v 51 Le maître le punira terriblement et le mettra avec les hypocrites. Là, ils pleureront et grinceront des dents.

sw.L: Lakini kama mtumwa huyo mwovu atasema ndani ya moyo wake, 'Bwana wangu anachelewa,' \v 49 kisha aanze kuwapiga watumwa wenzake, na kula na kunywa pamoja na wale wanaolewa, \v 50 bwana wa mtumwa huyo atafika siku ambayo hamtarajii, na saa ambayo haijui, \v 51 naye atampasua vipande viwili na kumpa sehemu yake pamoja na wanafiki; huko kutakuwa na kulia na kusaga meno.
sw.B: Lakini huenda mtumishi huyo akawa mwovu. Akajisemea moyoni, 'Bwana wangu anakawia sana kurudi,' \v 49 akaanza kuwapiga watumishi wenzake, huku akila na kunywa pamoja na walevi. \v 50 Ikiwa hivyo, bwana wake atakuja siku ambayo hamtazamii, na saa ambayo hajui. \v 51 Bwana huyo atamkata vipande vipande na kumweka pamoja na wanafiki, mahali ambapo watu watalia na kusaga meno.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme mtumishi huyo ni mbaya. Anajisemea, 'Bwana wangu hatarudi hivi karibuni.' \v 49 Kwa hiyo anaanza kuwapiga watumishi wengine. Anakula na kunywa pamoja na watu wanaolewa. \v 50 Kisha bwana wake atarudi siku ambayo mtumishi huyo hamtarajii, saa ambayo hajui. \v 51 Bwana huyo atamwadhibu vikali sana na kumweka pamoja na wanafiki. Huko watalia na kusaga meno.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu nô lệ gian ác ấy nói trong lòng: 'Chủ ta chậm đến,' \v 49 và bắt đầu đánh các bạn nô lệ của mình, và ăn uống với những kẻ say sưa, \v 50 thì chủ của nô lệ ấy sẽ đến vào ngày hắn không trông đợi và vào giờ hắn không biết, \v 51 và sẽ phân thây hắn và đặt phần của hắn với những kẻ đạo đức giả; ở đó sẽ có khóc lóc và nghiến răng.
vi.B: Nhưng nếu người đầy tớ ấy gian ác và nghĩ thầm: 'Chủ ta còn lâu mới về,' \v 49 rồi bắt đầu đánh đập các bạn đầy tớ, ăn uống với những kẻ say sưa, \v 50 thì chủ của hắn sẽ đến vào ngày hắn không ngờ, vào giờ hắn không biết. \v 51 Chủ sẽ xé xác hắn và bắt hắn chịu chung số phận với những kẻ đạo đức giả, là nơi người ta sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.
vi.R: Nhưng giả sử người đầy tớ ấy là người xấu. Hắn nghĩ thầm: 'Chủ ta còn lâu mới trở về.' \v 49 Vì thế hắn bắt đầu đánh đập các đầy tớ khác. Hắn ăn uống với những kẻ say rượu. \v 50 Rồi ông chủ sẽ trở về vào một ngày hắn không ngờ, vào lúc hắn không biết. \v 51 Ông chủ sẽ trừng phạt hắn thật nặng và đưa hắn đến ở chung với những kẻ đạo đức giả. Ở đó người ta sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.

ko.L: 그러나 만일 그 악한 종이 마음속으로 '내 주인이 늦어진다' 하고 말하며, \v 49 자기 동료 종들을 때리기 시작하고, 술 취한 사람들과 함께 먹고 마시면, \v 50 그 종의 주인이 그가 기대하지 않은 날, 그가 알지 못하는 때에 와서, \v 51 그를 둘로 쪼개고, 그의 몫을 위선자들과 함께 둘 것이다. 거기에는 울음과 이를 가는 일이 있을 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 그 종이 악한 종이어서 속으로 '주인이 오려면 아직 멀었다' 하고 생각하며, \v 49 동료 종들을 때리기 시작하고 술꾼들과 어울려 먹고 마신다고 하자. \v 50 그러면 그 종의 주인이 그가 생각하지도 않은 날, 알지도 못하는 때에 돌아와서, \v 51 그를 몹시 쳐서 토막 내고, 위선자들과 같은 벌을 받게 할 것이다. 거기서 그는 울며 이를 갈 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 그 종이 악한 종이라고 하자. 그는 속으로 '주인은 한참 동안 돌아오지 않을 거야' 하고 생각한다. \v 49 그래서 다른 종들을 때리기 시작한다. 술에 취한 사람들과 함께 먹고 마신다. \v 50 그러면 주인은 그 종이 생각하지도 못한 날, 알지도 못하는 때에 돌아올 것이다. \v 51 주인은 그 종을 아주 무섭게 벌하고, 위선자들이 가는 곳으로 보낼 것이다. 거기서 사람들은 울며 이를 갈 것이다.

am.L: ያ ክፉ ባሪያ ግን በልቡ፦ “ጌታዬ ይዘገያል” ቢል፣ \v 49 ባልንጀሮቹን ባሪያዎች መደብደብ ቢጀምር፣ ከሰካራሞችም ጋር ቢበላና ቢጠጣ፣ \v 50 የዚያ ባሪያ ጌታ ባልጠበቀው ቀንና ባላወቀው ሰዓት ይመጣል፤ \v 51 ለሁለትም ይቆርጠዋል፤ ድርሻውንም ከግብዞች ጋር ይመድብለታል፤ በዚያ ለቅሶና ጥርስ ማፋጨት ይሆናል።
am.B: ያ አገልጋይ ግን ክፉ ሊሆን ይችላል። በልቡ “ጌታዬ ሳይመጣ ብዙ ጊዜ ይቆያል” ብሎ ያስብ ይሆናል፤ \v 49 ባልንጀሮቹን አገልጋዮች መደብደብ ይጀምራል፤ ከሰካራሞችም ጋር ይበላል፤ ይጠጣልም። \v 50 እንደዚህ ከሆነ ጌታው ባልጠበቀው ቀንና ባላወቀው ሰዓት ይመጣል። \v 51 ጌታውም ቆራርጦ ከግብዞች ጋር ያደርገዋል፤ በዚያም ሰዎች ያለቅሳሉ፤ ጥርሳቸውንም ያፋጫሉ።
am.R: ነገር ግን ያ አገልጋይ ክፉ ነው እንበል። በልቡ “ጌታዬ ለረጅም ጊዜ አይመለስም” ይላል። \v 49 ስለዚህ ሌሎቹን አገልጋዮች መደብደብ ይጀምራል። ከሚሰክሩ ሰዎች ጋር ይበላል፤ ይጠጣልም። \v 50 ከዚያም ጌታው አገልጋዩ ባልጠበቀው ቀን፣ ባላወቀውም ሰዓት ይመለሳል። \v 51 ጌታውም በጽኑ ይቀጣዋል፤ ከግብዞችም ጋር ያደርገዋል። በዚያም ያለቅሳሉ፤ ጥርሳቸውንም ያፋጫሉ።

decisions.choice: that evil slave: the same slave of 24:45, if he turns out wicked
decisions.reason: "That" points back to the slave put in charge. The same position can be used faithfully or abused.

decisions.choice: cut him in two: the severest punishment
alternatives: cut him off from the household
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut in two, a known form of execution. Yet the slave is then given a place with the hypocrites, so many read it as a picture of severe punishment, or as being cut off from the master's people.

decisions.choice: weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, the words picture the grief and rage of those shut out of the kingdom. Matthew repeats the phrase (13:42, 50; 22:13; 25:30).

decisions.choice: the hypocrites: those whose devotion is a pretense
decisions.reason: As in 6:2 and chapter 23, the word means people who act a part. The slave served his master in name but not in deed.

decisions.choice: where people will weep and grind their teeth (B); There they will cry and grind their teeth (R)
alternatives: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
decisions.reason: The wording of 8:12 is kept at each level.

decisions.choice: cut him in pieces (B); punish him terribly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture. Readable gives its meaning, following the meaning decision; if the picture means being cut off, "punish" still holds.

decisions.choice: My master is a long time coming (B); My master will not come back for a long time (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the delay means to the slave: he thinks there is plenty of time.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: ses compagnons d’esclavage (L); ses compagnons de service (B)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:7: Literal keeps that they were slaves with him, Balanced says they served the same master.

decisions.choice: "phân thây" (L); "xé xác" (B); "trừng phạt hắn thật nặng" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is "cut in two", the severest punishment (footnoted meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep the picture in Vietnamese words for it, Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "hắn" for the wicked servant; "kẻ đạo đức giả"; "khóc lóc và nghiến răng"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks the narrator's judgment in its pronouns: the servant who turns wicked becomes "hắn". The hypocrites and the weeping and gnashing of teeth keep the words of 6:2, 22:13 and 8:12.

decisions.choice: "둘로 쪼개다" (L); "몹시 쳐서 토막 내다" (B); "아주 무섭게 벌하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "cut in two", the severest punishment (meaning decision, footnoted); Literal keeps the picture, Balanced keeps its violence as the English Balanced does, Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: "위선자들"; "울음과 이를 가는 일" (L), "울며 이를 갈다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "위선자" is settled for the Korean Matthew; the closing words are those of the Korean Matthew 8:12 and 22:13.

decisions.choice: The servant's thought in the casual style "돌아오지 않을 거야" (R)
decisions.reason: He talks to himself carelessly; Readable lets the casual ending show it. Literal and Balanced keep the plain style.

decisions.choice: "ለቅሶና ጥርስ ማፋጨት" (weeping and gnashing of teeth, L); "ያለቅሳሉ፤ ጥርሳቸውንም ያፋጫሉ" (they weep and grind their teeth, B, R)
alternatives: explaining the gesture as anger or pain
decisions.reason: Grinding the teeth is a gesture Amharic knows for anguish and helpless rage, so the picture is kept at every level; Balanced and Readable make it a clause with a subject, as the English does.
